title: Do LLMs Hold Their Values? MANTA: A Multi-Turn Adversarial Benchmark for Animal Welfare Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2605.16301v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Evaluating animal welfare reasoning in LLMs remains an open challenge despite rapid deployment in consumer and professional contexts where welfare considerations appear implicitly in everyday queries. Existing benchmarks such as AnimalHarmBench evaluate this through single-turn, explicitly framed questions, measuring whether models avoid harmful content when directly asked. This approach overlooks two failure modes: alignment degradation under sustained adversarial pressure, and moral sensitivity (whether a model spontaneously surfaces welfare stakes in everyday queries). To fill this gap, we construct MANTA, a benchmark of 1,088 five-turn conversations progressing from an implicit Turn-1 scenario through an explicit welfare prompt to three adversarial pressure rounds drawn from a five-type taxonomy: Social, Cultural, Economic, Pragmatic, and Epistemic. translated_abstract: 尽管大语言模型已被快速部署于消费者和专业场景中，而在这类场景下，福利考量往往隐含于日常查询之中，但评估大语言模型的动物福利推理仍是一个悬而未决的挑战。现有基准测试（如 AnimalHarmBench）通过单轮、明确框架化的问题进行评估，衡量模型在被直接询问时是否避免产生有害内容。这种方法忽略了两种失效模式：一是持续对抗压力下的对齐退化，二是道德敏感性（即模型是否会在日常查询中自发地呈现福利相关利害关系）。为填补这一空白，我们构建了 MANTA——一个包含 1,088 段五轮对话的基准测试，对话从隐含的第一轮场景开始，经由明确的福利提示，再到三轮对抗压力回合，这些对抗压力源自一个五类分类法：社会型、文化型、经济型、实用型和认知型。我们从两个维度对对话进行评分：动物福利价值观稳定性（A
tldr: 该论文提出了 MANTA 基准，通过 1,088 段五轮多轮对抗对话评估大语言模型在动物福利推理中的价值观稳定性与道德敏感性，弥补了现有单轮基准无法检测持续对抗压力下对齐退化及道德敏感性缺失的不足。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces MANTA, a multi-turn adversarial benchmark of 1,088 five-turn conversations for evaluating LLMs' animal welfare value stability and moral sensitivity, addressing the limitations of single-turn benchmarks that overlook alignment degradation under sustained adversarial pressure.
